summary.title: CNNs, Part 1: An Introduction to Convolutional Neural Networks
summary.one_liner: You learn what convolutional neural networks are, how convolution, pooling and softmax layers work, and how to implement a forward pass of a small MNIST CNN from scratch in Python with numpy.
keywords: why not fully connected network for images
takeaways: Convolutional layers slide small filters over an image, multiplying and summing overlapping values to detect localized features such as edges.
Padding controls output size: valid padding shrinks width and height, while same padding keeps them equal to the input.
Max pooling with pool size 2 halves width and height by keeping the maximum value in each 2x2 block, pruning redundant information.
A softmax output layer turns scores into probabilities, which enables cross-entropy loss for training and measuring confidence.
The post implements a Conv3x3 layer, a MaxPool2 layer and a Softmax layer in numpy and runs a forward pass on MNIST, with the untrained network performing at random-guess level.
summary.summary: The article explains why CNNs suit image tasks: fully connected networks need huge numbers of weights for large images and react poorly to shifted positions. It then walks through convolution with a worked 4x4 example, Sobel edge filters, padding, conv layers, and max pooling. The author implements Conv3x3, MaxPool2 and Softmax classes in numpy and assembles a forward pass that classifies MNIST digits, showing near-random accuracy before training. Training and backpropagation are deferred to Part 2.
